descriptions.value: PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

descriptions.value: PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).

descriptions.value: Umbraco CMS 17.0.0 before 17.7.1 and 18.0.0 before 18.2.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in Management API document version endpoints that skip per-document ContentPermissionByResource checks. Authenticated back-office users restricted to a start node can list and read document versions outside their tree by GUID, exposing unpublished values and altering prevent-cleanup flags.

cna.title: PostgreSQL reindexdb index name quoting allows SQL injection

descriptions.value: SQL injection in PostgreSQL reindexdb allows an object creator to execute arbitrary SQL as the database user running reindexdb, via a crafted index name embedded in the parallel catalog query for --jobs with --index.  Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 and 17.12 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.

descriptions.description: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

configurations.value: victim runs reindexdb with --jobs and --index for an attacker-named index

credits.value: The PostgreSQL project thanks Anthropic OSS program for reporting this problem.

cna.title: PostgreSQL parallel RECORD typmod use-after-free executes arbitrary code

descriptions.value: Use after free in PostgreSQL coordination of anonymous RECORD type identifiers among parallel workers allows a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via causing one process to free a shared tuple descriptor while another process retains and later uses its address.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

descriptions.description: Use After Free
Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')

credits.value: The PostgreSQL project thanks Peter Geoghegan for reporting this problem.

cna.title: PostgreSQL composite-type change during field assignment executes arbitrary code

Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

descriptions.description: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')

credits.value: The PostgreSQL project thanks OpenAI Codex Security, Bronson Yen, and Mehmet D. INCE for reporting this problem.

cna.title: PostgreSQL plperl prepared-query use-after-free executes arbitrary code

descriptions.value: Use after free in PostgreSQL plperl allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via re-entering plperl and freeing a prepared query while an outer invocation is executing it.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

descriptions.description: Use After Free

configurations.value: Attacker has permission to "CREATE EXTENSION plperl", or another user previously issued that.  Attacker has permission to create objects (temporary objects or non-temporary objects in at least one schema).

credits.value: The PostgreSQL project thanks Zheng Yu for reporting this problem.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix tree connection use-after-free in smb2_tree_connect()

ksmbd_tree_conn_connect() publishes a new tree connection in
sess->tree_conns with a single reference and returns its pointer to
smb2_tree_connect(). The handler continues to initialize the object and
build the response after publication. A concurrent session logoff can
erase the connection and drop that reference, freeing the object while
the handler still uses it.

BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in smb2_tree_connect+0xe3d/0xf90
  smb2_tree_connect (fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c:2872)
  handle_ksmbd_work
  process_one_work
  worker_thread
  kthread

After xa_store() succeeds, take a second reference before releasing
tree_conns_lock. The original reference belongs to the xarray entry and
the second belongs to the creating smb2_tree_connect() handler.

Keep the references balanced in every path:

- On normal exit or an error after publication, smb2_tree_connect()
  drops its creator reference. Error cleanup also calls
  ksmbd_tree_conn_disconnect(), which drops the xarray reference only if
  it removes the exact entry.
- SMB2 TREE_DISCONNECT uses the same helper to remove the entry and drop
  its xarray reference. The request's existing lookup reference remains
  owned by the request and is released by the existing cleanup.
- Session LOGOFF removes each entry and drops its xarray reference. If
  it wins the race, later cleanup sees that the entry is gone and does
  not drop that reference again.

To enforce this ownership, claim the disconnected state and erase the
exact entry atomically under tree_conns_lock. This guarantees one drop
for the xarray reference and one drop by each in-flight user, regardless
of which teardown path wins. If logoff removes the entry before
initialization completes, fail the connect instead of marking the
detached object TREE_CONNECTED.

scenarios.value:
AV:N - ksmbd is the in-kernel SMB server on TCP/445; the UAF is reached from remote SMB2 TREE_CONNECT racing SESSION_LOGOFF via ksmbd_conn_handler_loop() through handle_ksmbd_work(), smb2_tree_connect(), ksmbd_tree_conn_connect(), and ksmbd_tree_conn_session_logoff().
AC:L - The attacker drives both sides by issuing concurrent SMB2 TREE_CONNECT and SESSION_LOGOFF on their own connections (SMB3 multi-channel or parallel ksmbd-io work items). After xa_store() the object has one xarray ref, so logoff can free it while the handler still uses it; no victim timing or rare kernel config is required.
PR:N - TREE_CONNECT and LOGOFF need a valid SMB2 session, but ksmbd supports guest/anonymous users and guest-ok shares (including IPC$); guest session setup skips NTLMSSP password verification, so a reasonable NAS/IoT deployment lets an unauthenticated client reach this path.
UI:N - No victim action is required; the attacker programmatically issues SESSION_SETUP, TREE_CONNECT, and LOGOFF on their own SMB connections to trigger the race.
S:U - The UAF corrupts ksmbd/kernel heap on the SMB server host and can escalate privileges within that kernel; it does not cross a VM, guest-to-host, container, or IOMMU/DMA security boundary.
C:H - Use-after-free of struct ksmbd_tree_connect and its share_conf pointer: after logoff kfree's the published object, smb2_tree_connect still reads share flags and fields, enabling arbitrary kernel disclosure via heap reuse.
I:H - The handler writes t_state, maximal_access, and posix_extensions into the freed object after xa_store(); with heap spray this yields arbitrary kernel writes and control-flow hijacking, matching High integrity for tree_conn UAF.
A:H - KASAN reports slab-use-after-free in smb2_tree_connect on the ksmbd-io worker; the dangling tree_conn pointer causes a kernel oops or panic and is repeatable by resending TREE_CONNECT concurrently with LOGOFF.

cna.title: ksmbd: fix tree connection use-after-free in smb2_tree_connect()

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xen-netback: defer xenvif_mcast_addr_list_free()

In order for the function to legitimately avoid locking/RCU, it needs to
run after all TX/RX processing has finished/stopped: Lookups happen from
xenvif_start_xmit(), while adds/removes happen from xenvif_tx_action()
(called out of xenvif_poll()).

Move the call out of xenvif_disconnect_data() (the call to the function
from connect()'s error path doesn't require any cleaning up there), and
put it past the synchronization point in backend_disconnect().

This is XSA-527 / CVE-2026-100081.

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The guest reaches the free by changing xenbus state: frontend_changed() calls set_backend_state(), which from XenbusStateConnected calls backend_disconnect() and xenvif_disconnect_data(), where xenvif_mcast_addr_list_free() ran before synchronize_net(). The raced lookup is xenvif_mcast_match() inside xenvif_start_xmit(); the trigger is that xenbus write, not a routable packet field.
AC:H - xenvif_mcast_match() runs only when xenvif_start_xmit() has already seen VIF_STATUS_CONNECTED and a live queue->task, but xenvif_mcast_addr_list_free() runs only after xenvif_carrier_off() clears that bit and xenvif_disconnect_queue() returns from kthread_stop(). The lookup does not sleep, so it must be stalled across that teardown; MCAST_ADD plus Closing does not create that stall, and napi_disable() has already finished xenvif_tx_action().
PR:L - frontend_changed() is the vif backend otherend_changed callback and accepts any connected frontend. The attacker must control that guest's xenstore frontend state and TX ring, i.e. the guest kernel; a host user namespace has no path to this xenbus backend.
UI:N - The guest writes its own request-multicast-control key, queues XEN_NETIF_EXTRA_TYPE_MCAST_ADD on the TX ring, and sets the frontend xenbus state to Closing. The host operator does not have to mount media, open a device, or acknowledge a prompt.
S:C - The use-after-free is in dom0 xen-netback: xenvif_mcast_match() dereferences vif->fe_mcast_addr nodes freed by xenvif_mcast_addr_list_free(). A guest that wins the race crashes or corrupts that backend kernel, crossing the Xen guest-to-host boundary.
C:H - xenvif_mcast_match() walks fe_mcast_addr under rcu_read_lock() via list_for_each_entry_rcu() and ether_addr_equal() on mcast->addr, while xenvif_mcast_addr_list_free() kfree()s those xenvif_mcast_addr nodes with no grace period. A reused node lets the walk follow next pointers into other kernel memory.
I:H - The freed objects are slab allocations from kzalloc_obj() in xenvif_mcast_add(). xenvif_mcast_match() can still dereference them after kfree() in xenvif_mcast_addr_list_free(), a heap use-after-free in the backend rather than a NULL deref, and XSA-527 treats host privilege escalation from that race as possible.
A:H - A list walk in xenvif_mcast_match() that follows an fe_mcast_addr node already passed to kfree() by xenvif_mcast_addr_list_free() oopses the backend kernel. XSA-527 describes that fault as a driver crash that can take down the host.

cna.title: Elementor < 4.3.6 - Contributor+ Stored XSS via Element ID

descriptions.description: CWE-79 Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)

descriptions.value: The Elementor Website Builder  WordPress plugin before 4.3.6 does not validate or escape an element identifier before rendering it into a client-side framework attribute that is evaluated as JavaScript, allowing users with the Contributor role to store scripts that execute in the browser of anyone viewing the affected content, including an administrator reviewing the submission for publication.

descriptions.description: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
